title: Adminlets: composable admin utilities and execution fabric for support automation
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem: onboarding and operating ad-hoc admin scripts has caused repeated toil and unsafe emergency changes. We need a small, composable runtime for short-lived, idempotent admin utilities ("adminlets") that can be executed from the Console, CI, or triggered by incidents, with strong auditability and safe defaults.

Goal: design and ship an 'adminlets' execution fabric that lets engineers author typed, idempotent admin utilities (node-level and control-plane actions) as packageable artifacts; expose them as first-class runbook steps in the runbooks-as-tasks flow; and instrument them with structured telemetry, RBAC, and automatic dry-run capability.

Scope: authoring API/SDK, execution orchestration, RBAC integration, audit/logging, metrics, Console UI for selection and canary parameters.

Non-goals: full general-purpose scripting shell (we intentionally restrict to pre-approved primitives and vetted adminlets), long-running background jobs (scheduled batch jobs are out of scope).
acceptance_criteria: Engineers can register a new adminlet bundle via GH PR and a CI task validates idempotency checks and schema (schema link in attachments).
Console can render available adminlets with descriptions, input schemas, suggested defaults, and one-click dry-run and execute actions restricted by RBAC.
Every adminlet execution produces a structured audit event (user/service, parameters, result, exit-code, duration) persisted to the audit-log cluster and visible in Console activity feed.
A safe-execution mode prevents adminlets from making changes when invoked during high-severity incidents unless escalation is approved (policy-driven).
Canary rollout mechanics: start at 1% of traffic (for automated triggers) and provide manual canary controls for manual executions.
Integration tests coverage >= 85% for core orchestration and failure modes (permission denied, timeouts, partial failures).
design_decisions: Model adminlets as lightweight containerized functions with a typed manifest (inputs, outputs, idempotency_token optional).
No interactive shell: adminlets accept inputs via JSON schema; outputs must be structured JSON for traceability.
Authorization: adminlets execute with a 'least-privilege' ops-service principal; Console enforces per-adminlet allowlists mapped to SSO groups.
All invocations write an immutable audit entry and optional rich trace to the tracing backend (OTLP => internal tracing cluster).
Idempotency: prefer declarative primitives (change desired-state) and include automatic retry with exponential backoff for transient failures.
implementation_notes: Prototype runtime: lightweight Go service (adminlets-runner) with gRPC API for orchestration; will containerize with distroless image.
Schema/validator lib: use existing runtime schema library (see GH: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infer-runtime/tree/main/schema).
PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ops-adminlets/pull/234 implements manifest parser and local dry-run harness.
Design doc: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/OPS/pages/123456/Adminlets+Design (sequence diagrams, threat model, audit format).
Grafana dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.company/d/ops/adminlets-executions (executions by status, latency, error-class).
Storage: audit events will go to audit-log cluster S3 bucket with gzip+parquet nightly compaction for retention and searchability.
rollout_plan: Alpha: internal devs only (teams: infra, support) - 2 weeks of testing with manual triggers and elevated logging.
Beta: add Canary policy: automated incident-triggered adminlets restricted to 'read-only' subset; manual execution requires explicit approval in Console.
GA: enable adminlets in Console for all SSO groups with RBAC mapping and add to runbooks-as-tasks library.
Fallback: ability to immediately revoke adminlet execution via feature-flag for emergency kill-switch.
testing_plan: Unit tests for manifest parsing and schema validation (CI gate).
Integration tests: runner + auth + audit pipeline in staging; simulate transient infra failures and assert retries and eventual consistency.
Chaos tests: force partial network partitions to ensure adminlets either complete or surface safe errors (no partial destructive state).
Security pen-test: scoped review of principle-of-least-privilege mappings and audit integrity.
